marble.name: Gas Exchange & Breathing
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Describe the structure of the human gas exchange system (trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli) and explain how the mechanism of breathing — using pressure changes from rib and diaphragm movement — moves air in and out of the lungs
marble.prompt: If you took a deep breath after running, could they explain what's happening in their lungs — how the air gets in, where the oxygen crosses into the blood, and how carbon dioxide leaves?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about the amazing diversity of life — identifying different animals and plants, understanding how body parts help animals survive, and discovering what all living things need to stay alive.

misconceptions: Thinking air is actively 'sucked' in by the lungs rather than pushed in by higher outside pressure when chest volume increases.
Believing lungs contain muscle that inflates them (ventilation is driven by diaphragm and intercostal muscles; lungs are passive).
Confusing breathing with respiration, or thinking gas exchange and breathing are the same thing.
Thinking only oxygen moves (forgetting CO₂ diffuses the other way).
Assuming gas exchange happens all along the airways rather than at the alveoli.
representations: Labelled lung/airway diagram (trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli)
Bell-jar / diaphragm-and-balloon pressure model of ventilation
Alveolus–capillary close-up showing O₂ in, CO₂ out with adaptations labelled
Pressure–volume relationship diagram for inhalation vs exhalation
authoredAnswer: Exhaled air still contains plenty of oxygen (roughly 16%, only a few percent less than the ~21% inhaled) — only some of the oxygen diffuses across the thin alveoli into the blood in exchange for carbon dioxide; breathing itself is caused by pressure changes when the ribs and diaphragm move, not by the lungs sucking.
probe: Compare a small candle flame in a jar of room air with one in a jar the child has breathed into (or have them exhale gently near a sheltered flame). Before the demonstration, ask them to predict whether a flame can still burn in exhaled air and WHY. The reason is diagnostic: a child believing exhaled air is pure CO2 pr

wrongAnswers.fix: give the real figures (inhaled ~21% O2, exhaled ~16%); only some oxygen diffuses out and exhaled air is still mostly nitrogen with plenty of oxygen — which is why rescue breaths work

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: reason says the lungs pull or suck the air in themselves
wrongAnswers.fix: reattribute breathing to pressure change: ribs and diaphragm enlarge the chest, lowering the pressure so higher outside air pressure pushes air in; the lungs are passive

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: probe reveals air routed to the stomach, or no notion that gas passes into the blood at the alveoli
wrongAnswers.fix: trace the path trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli, and the thin alveolar wall where oxygen diffuses into the blood capillaries

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: explains oxygen being pushed or pumped into the blood
wrongAnswers.fix: link back to diffusion down a concentration gradient across the alveolar surface; the adaptations (large area, thin walls, good blood supply) speed it up

before.name: Cells to Organ Systems
before.reason: The gas exchange system is an organ system — hierarchy concept provides structural context

before.name: How Diffusion Works
before.reason: Gas exchange at the alveoli is driven by diffusion — the mechanism must be understood first
